title: The Flannan Isles Mystery
hook: In 1900, three lighthouse keepers vanished without a trace from a remote Scottish island.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: Their lighthouse stood alone on a rock, battered by an Atlantic storm.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Inside, the clock had stopped ticking, and the beds lay unmade.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Two sets of oilskins were gone, yet one still hung inside despite the storm.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Investigators found ropes and equipment torn away, high above the crashing sea.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: The official theory says a huge rogue wave swept the men to their deaths.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: No wreckage, no bodies, and no witnesses were ever found again on that island.

end.line: What really happened to the keepers of Flannan Isles?

description: In December 1900, three lighthouse keepers vanished from a remote Scottish island, leaving a stopped clock and an empty lighthouse behind.

facts.claim: Three lighthouse keepers, James Ducat, Thomas Marshall, and Donald MacArthur, disappeared from the Flannan Isles Lighthouse in December 1900.
The relief vessel Hesperus arrived on 26 December 1900 and found the lighthouse deserted, with the entrance gate and door closed.
Inside, the clock had stopped and one bed appeared not to have been slept in recently.
facts.source: Northern Lighthouse Board records, cited in Wikipedia

facts.claim: One set of oilskins was missing, suggesting a keeper left without waterproof clothing.
Official investigator Robert Muirhead concluded storm-damaged ropes and equipment at the West Landing pointed to the men being swept away by a large wave.
No trace of the three men was ever found despite extensive searches.
Later popular accounts added eerie details, such as an untouched meal, that do not appear in the original investigation records.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Flannan Isles Lighthouse; "Flannan Isle" poem by Wilfrid Wilson Gibson, 1912
